question: Should OpenClaw add task-level model metadata to HEARTBEAT.md, or should heartbeat task routing stay whole-turn/plugin-owned unless a broader routing contract is designed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation changes public HEARTBEAT.md syntax and model-routing semantics, and automation should not choose split-versus-batched execution or provider fallback behavior on its own.

options.title: Design shared routing contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and decide reusable heartbeat or per-turn routing semantics before accepting HEARTBEAT.md-only syntax.

options.title: Add heartbeat-only task metadata
options.body: Implement a narrow HEARTBEAT.md task model field with explicit split/group semantics, alias/fallback rules, docs, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep routing plugin-owned
options.body: Document whole-turn before_model_resolve plugins as the supported routing path and accept that multiple due heartbeat tasks cannot be independently routed today.

recommendation.title: Design shared routing contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and decide reusable heartbeat or per-turn routing semantics before accepting HEARTBEAT.md-only syntax.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest combined history is across the model hook seam, heartbeat task batching, and product-boundary decisions for config/routing surfaces.
